chapterNote: Chapter 3 gathers the son into the heart of the matter: a life wholly entrusted to the LORD. It opens with paired calls to keep the father's teaching for long life and favor (vv. 1-4), rises to the book's most quoted summons — trust the LORD with the whole heart and let Him straighten your paths (vv. 5-8), then turns this trust toward the wallet (honor Him with your wealth, vv. 9-10) and toward the rod (welcome His discipline as a Father's love, vv. 11-12). A great hymn to Wisdom follows, prizing her above gold and tracing her back to creation itself, where the LORD founded the earth by wisdom (vv. 13-20). The chapter closes with a portrait of the wise man's settled, fearless rest (vv. 21-26) and a cluster of neighbor-love commands, sealed by the LORD's two-sided verdict on the perverse and the upright (vv. 27-35).

1.text: My son, do not forget my teaching; let your heart guard my commandments closely,
1.amp: My son [ben], do not forget [shakach — let slip from mind, neglect] my teaching [torah — instruction, the same word as 'Law']; but let your heart [leb] keep [natsar — watch over, guard like a sentry] my commandments [mitsvah],
1.notes: torah (H8451) here is the father's instruction, carrying the full weight of the word used for God's own Law; natsar (H5341) is the verb for posting a guard. The son is not merely to remember the teaching but to mount watch over it in the heart — the inner command-post of the whole life. Also tagged: ben (H1121), shakach (H7911), leb (H3820), mitsvah (H4687).

2.text: for they will lengthen your days and add years of life and peace to you.
2.amp: for length [orek] of days [yom] and years [shanah] of life [chay] and peace [shalom — wholeness, well-being, nothing missing] they will add [yasaph — pile on, increase] to you.
2.notes: shalom (H7965) is far more than the absence of conflict — it is wholeness, a life with nothing broken and nothing lacking; yasaph (H3254) means to keep adding. Obedience does not merely avoid harm but actively heaps up length of days and well-being (cf. Eph 6:2-3). Also tagged: orek (H753), yom (H3117), shanah (H8141), chay (H2416).

3.text: Do not let steadfast love and faithfulness leave you; bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart.
3.amp: Let not mercy [chesed — steadfast covenant love, loyal kindness] and truth [emeth — faithfulness, reliability] forsake [azab — abandon, let go of] you; bind them about your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart [leb].
3.notes: chesed (H2617) and emeth (H571) are the twin pillars of God's own character (Ex 34:6) — loyal love and unfailing truthfulness — here to be worn and inscribed by the son. To write them on the leb (H3820) anticipates the new covenant promise of the law written on the heart (Jer 31:33). Also tagged: azab (H5800).

4.text: So you will find favor and a good name in the eyes of God and of men.
4.amp: So you will find [matsa — attain, light upon] favor [chen — grace, gracious acceptance] and good [tov] understanding [sekhel — good sense, the kind of insight that wins esteem] in the sight [ayin — the eyes] of God [Elohim] and man [adam].
4.notes: chen (H2580) is unearned favor; sekel (H7922) is prudent good sense that, lived out, earns a good reputation. The pairing 'God and man' (cf. Luke 2:52 of the boy Jesus) marks a life that is right both upward toward heaven and outward toward the watching community. Also tagged: matsa (H4672), tov (H2896), ayin (H5869), Elohim (H430), adam (H120).

5.text: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not rest your weight on your own understanding.
5.amp: Trust [batach — lean your whole confidence on, rely utterly] in the LORD [YHWH] with all your heart [leb]; and lean [shaan — prop yourself, rest your weight] not on your own understanding [binah — your own power to figure things out].
5.notes: batach (H982) is to throw the full weight of one's confidence onto something; shaan (H8172) pictures a man propping himself on a staff. The contrast is total: rest everything on the LORD, nothing on your own binah (H998). Not the rejection of thought, but the refusal to make one's own reasoning the final ground. Also tagged: YHWH (H3068), leb (H3820).

6.text: In all your ways, know Him, and He will direct your paths.
6.amp: In all your ways [derek] know Him [yada — know by relationship, reckon with Him intimately], and He will direct [yashar — make level, straight, set right] your paths [orach].
6.notes: yada (H3045) is to know by relationship, not bare acknowledgment — to bring God into reckoning in every road one walks; yashar (H3474) means to make level or straight. The promise is not an easy road but a rightly-directed one: He clears and aligns the path of the one who walks it consciously before Him. Also tagged: derek (H1870), orach (H734).

7.text: Never let your own eyes pronounce you wise; stand in awe of the LORD, and swerve away from evil.
7.amp: Do not be wise [khakham] in your own eyes [ayin]; fear [yare — stand in reverent awe of] the LORD [YHWH], and turn aside [sur — depart, swerve away] from evil [ra].
7.notes: this verse inverts the great theme: the fear of the LORD (yare, H3372) drives out self-conceit, the wisdom that is 'in one's own eyes.' To fear the LORD truly is to actively turn (sur, H5493) from evil — reverence and repentance are the same motion. Health for the body follows in v.8 (cf. 3:13; 26:12). Also tagged: khakham (H2450), ayin (H5869), YHWH (H3068), ra (H7451).

8.text: It will be healing to your body and refreshing moisture to your bones.
8.amp: It will be health [riphuth — a healing, a medicine] to your navel [shor — the body, here the seat of vitality], and marrow [shiqquy — moistening, refreshment] to your bones [etsem].
8.notes: the Hebrew literally reads 'medicine to your navel and watering to your bones' — vivid bodily images for deep, renewing health. The fear of the LORD that turns from evil (v.7) is not abstract piety; it works down into the very marrow, the frame of a man, making him whole. Also tagged: riphuth (H7500), shor (H8270), shiqquy (H8250), etsem (H6106).

9.text: Give weight to the LORD out of your wealth — let the first and best of every harvest be His;
9.amp: Honor [kabad — give weight to, treat as heavy with worth] the LORD [YHWH] with your wealth [hon — riches, substance], and with the firstfruits [reshith — the first and best] of all your increase [tevuah — harvest, yield];
9.notes: kabad (H3513) literally means to make heavy — to honor is to assign real weight to God, and the proof is the wallet. reshith (H7225) is the first and choicest portion (cf. Ex 23:19); giving God the first of the increase, not the leftovers, confesses that all of it came from Him. Also tagged: YHWH (H3068), hon (H1952), tevuah (H8393).

10.text: then your barns will be filled with abundance, and your vats will overflow with new wine.
10.amp: then your barns [asam — storehouses] will be filled [male] with plenty [sava — abundance, fullness], and your presses [yeqev — the wine vats] will burst [parats — break out, overflow] with new wine [tirosh — fresh grape juice, new wine].
10.notes: parats (H6555) means to break through or burst the bounds — the vats so full they overflow their walls. The promise is not a transaction that buys God's favor but the generous order of His covenant: the open hand toward God meets an overflowing return (cf. Mal 3:10; 2 Cor 9:6-8). Also tagged: asam (H618), male (H4390), sava (H7647), yeqev (H3342), tirosh (H8492).

11.text: My son, do not make light of the LORD's discipline, and do not grow weary when He corrects you;
11.amp: My son [ben], do not despise [maas — reject, treat as worthless] the chastening [musar — corrective discipline, formative instruction] of the LORD [YHWH]; nor be weary [quts — grow sick of, loathe] of His correction [tokhachat — reproof, rebuke];
11.notes: musar (H4148) is the discipline that shapes, and tokhachat (H8433) the reproof that corrects — both gifts, not punishments to resent. maas (H3988) is to spurn; the danger is twofold: to despise the rod as if it meant nothing, or to faint under it as if it meant rejection. Quoted in Heb 12:5-6. Also tagged: ben (H1121), YHWH (H3068), quts (H6973).

12.text: for the LORD reproves the one He loves, as a father corrects the son in whom he delights.
12.amp: for whom the LORD [YHWH] loves [ahab — loves, delights in] He reproves [yakach — corrects, sets right], even as a father [ab] the son [ben] in whom he delights [ratsah — takes pleasure in, accepts with favor].
12.notes: yakach (H3198) is to correct or set right; the proof of love is not the absence of discipline but its presence. ratsah (H7521) is the favor a father has toward a cherished child. Discipline is reframed as the surest sign of sonship, not its denial — the very logic Hebrews 12 draws on to comfort the suffering. Also tagged: YHWH (H3068), ahab (H157), ab (H1), ben (H1121).

13.text: Blessed is the one who finds wisdom, the one who comes into understanding,
13.amp: Happy [osher — blessed, in a state of true well-being] is the man [adam] who finds [matsa] wisdom [chokmah], and the man who gains [puq — draws out, obtains] understanding [tebunah];
13.notes: osher (H835) opens the great Wisdom-hymn of vv.13-18 with a beatitude: the truly blessed life is the one that has found chokmah (H2451). The kit notes the Hebrew of 'gets' carries the sense of drawing understanding out as from a well — wisdom is mined and drawn up, not handed over idle. Also tagged: adam (H120), matsa (H4672), puq (H6329), tebunah (H8394).

14.text: for the profit she brings is better than profit in silver, and her yield better than fine gold.
14.amp: for the gain [sachar — profit, merchandise, return] of her is better [tov] than the gain of silver [keseph], and her yield [tevuah — produce, return] than fine gold [charuts].
14.notes: the language is the merchant's ledger — sachar (H5504) is trading profit. Wisdom is weighed against the two great stores of value, silver (keseph, H3701) and refined gold (charuts, H2742), and outweighs them both. The comparison is not that she is priceless in theory but that she pays better in practice. Also tagged: tov (H2896), tevuah (H8393).

15.text: She is more precious than coral and jewels, and nothing you could desire can equal her.
15.amp: She is more precious [yaqar — rare, costly, of great worth] than rubies [peninim — corals, costly jewels]; and all the things you can desire [chephets — delight, what your heart longs for] cannot be set equal [shavah — compared, leveled, made even] to her.
15.notes: yaqar (H3368) is what is rare and costly; shavah (H7737) means to set on the same level. Whatever a man most desires (chephets, H2656) cannot be laid in the balance against wisdom and made to weigh the same. This couplet returns nearly word for word in 8:11. Also tagged: peninim (H6443).

16.text: Her right hand holds out length of days; with her left she offers riches and honor.
16.amp: Length [orek] of days [yom] is in her right hand [yamin]; and in her left hand riches [osher] and honor [kavod — weight, glory, esteem].
16.notes: Wisdom is pictured as a queen with full hands — the right hand, the place of strength and blessing, holds long life; the left holds wealth and kavod (H3519), honor. She gives what the world chases by other means, and gives it rightly, as the gift of the LORD who founded all things by her (v.19). Also tagged: orek (H753), yom (H3117), yamin (H3225), osher (H6239).

17.text: Her ways are pleasant ways, and all her paths lead to peace.
17.amp: Her ways [derek] are ways of pleasantness [noam — delight, loveliness, agreeableness], and all her paths [nathiv — well-trodden trails] are peace [shalom].
17.notes: noam (H5278) is delightful pleasantness; shalom (H7965) is the wholeness that crowns the journey. Wisdom's road is not a grim duty but a good way to walk — pleasant in the traveling and peaceful in the arriving. The discipline she requires opens onto rest, not deprivation. Also tagged: derek (H1870), nathiv (H5410).

18.text: She is a tree of life to those who take hold of her, and blessed are all who hold her fast.
18.amp: She is a tree [ets] of life [chay] to those who lay hold [chazaq — grasp firmly, take a strong grip] of her; and happy [ashar — blessed, called blessed] is everyone who keeps her fast [tamak — holds up, supports, will not let go].
18.notes: the 'tree of life' (ets chayyim) reaches back to Eden (Gen 2:9) and forward to the City of God (Rev 22:2): wisdom restores what was lost. chazaq (H2388) and tamak (H8551) are both grip-words — to find wisdom is not enough; one must seize her and hold on, and the holding itself is blessing. Also tagged: ets (H6086), chay (H2416), ashar (H833).

19.text: The LORD by wisdom founded the earth; by understanding He set the heavens in place.
19.amp: The LORD [YHWH] by wisdom [chokmah] founded [yasad — laid the foundation of] the earth [erets]; by understanding [tebunah] He established [kun — set firm, fixed in place] the heavens [shamayim].
19.notes: the hymn rises to its peak: the very wisdom the son is urged to seek is the wisdom by which God made the world. yasad (H3245) lays a foundation; kun (H3559) fixes firmly. To live by wisdom is to live with the grain of creation itself — it is woven into the structure of reality (cf. 8:22-31; Col 1:16). Also tagged: YHWH (H3068), chokmah (H2451), erets (H776), tebunah (H8394), shamayim (H8064).

20.text: By His knowledge the deep was split open, and the clouds drip down the dew.
20.amp: By His knowledge [daat] the depths [tehom — the deep, the primeval ocean-abyss] were broken open [baqa — cleaved, split apart], and the clouds [shechaqim — the skies] drop down [raaph — distill, trickle] the dew [tal].
20.notes: tehom (H8415) is the primeval deep of Gen 1:2; baqa (H1234) the splitting that brought forth springs and seas (cf. Gen 7:11). The same divine daat (H1847) that cleaved the great deep also tends the gentle dew — God's wisdom rules both the vast and the small, the violent waters and the quiet morning moisture. Also tagged: shechaqim (H7834), raaph (H7491), tal (H2919).

21.text: My son, do not let them slip from your sight; hold on to sound wisdom and discretion,
21.amp: My son [ben], let them not depart [luz — slip away, turn aside] from your eyes [ayin]; keep [natsar — guard, watch over] sound wisdom [tushiyyah — effective, success-bringing wisdom] and discretion [mezimmah — the foreseeing, planning mind];
21.notes: after the hymn, the address returns: natsar (H5341) is again the guard-verb of v.1. tushiyyah (H8454) is wisdom that actually works and endures, and mezimmah (H4209) the foresight that plans ahead — a 'gray' word that, ruled by wisdom, becomes protective shrewdness rather than scheming. Also tagged: ben (H1121), luz (H3868), ayin (H5869).

22.text: and they will be life to your soul and a graceful ornament for your neck.
22.amp: so they will be life [chay] to your soul [nephesh — your whole living self], and grace [chen — favor, an adornment of grace] to your neck.
22.notes: wisdom kept (v.21) repays the keeper: it becomes chay (H2416) to the nephesh (H5315), the inner life animated, and chen (H2580) to the neck, an ornament of favor visible to all. The neck-imagery echoes v.3 — what is bound on the neck and written on the heart becomes the soul's own life and beauty.

23.text: Then you will walk your road in safety, and your foot will not strike against a stone.
23.amp: Then you will walk [yalak] in your way [derek] securely [betach — in safety, confidence, without dread], and your foot [regel] will not stumble [nagaph — strike, dash against, be tripped].
23.notes: betach (H983) is settled security, the confidence of one with nothing to fear; nagaph (H5062) is to strike the foot, to be tripped into ruin. The wise man's walk is steady not because the road is smooth but because wisdom keeps his footing (cf. Ps 91:11-12, the same imagery of the guarded foot). Also tagged: yalak (H3212), derek (H1870), regel (H7272).

24.text: Lie down, and no dread will find you; you will stretch out to rest, and sweet will be your sleep.
24.amp: When you lie down [shakab], dread [pachad — trembling fear] will not touch you; yes, you will stretch out [shakab — lie down], and your sleep [shenah] will be sweet [arev — pleasant, agreeable].
24.notes: pachad (H6342) is the trembling dread that robs sleep; arev (H6149) is the sweetness of untroubled rest. The wise man's nights are as secure as his days — a conscience at rest under God's keeping sleeps soundly, free of the fears that haunt the guilty (cf. Ps 4:8; Lev 26:6). Also tagged: shakab (H7901), shenah (H8142).

25.text: Do not be afraid of sudden terror, nor of the storm that falls on the wicked when it comes,
25.amp: Do not be afraid [yare] of sudden [pithom] terror [pachad — dread, the thing that makes one tremble], nor of the desolation [shoah — devastation, ruin] of the wicked [rasha] when it comes [bo];
25.notes: shoah (H7722) is sweeping devastation — the ruin that overtakes the rasha (H7563). The wise man is told not to share the panic that grips the guilty when calamity strikes, for his security rests elsewhere. The fear-verb yare (H3372), used of the LORD in v.7, here is forbidden toward mere disaster: one fears God and so fears nothing else. Also tagged: pithom (H6597), pachad (H6343), bo (H935).

26.text: for the LORD will be your confidence, and He will keep your foot from being caught.
26.amp: for the LORD [YHWH] will be your confidence [kesel — your assurance, the ground of your trust], and will keep [shamar — guard, preserve] your foot [regel] from being taken [leked — capture, a being caught in a snare].
26.notes: the reason fear is unnecessary (v.25): the LORD Himself is the wise man's kesel (H3689), his confidence; shamar (H8104) is the sentry-keeping verb. leked (H3921) is capture itself, the being caught in a trap or snare — God guards the foot of His own from the nets the wicked fall into. The keeping is personal: not a principle but a Person stands guard. Also tagged: YHWH (H3068), regel (H7272).

27.text: Do not withhold good from those who deserve it, when it lies within your power to act.
27.amp: Do not withhold [mana — hold back, restrain] good [tov] from those to whom it is owed [baal — its owners, those who have a rightful claim to it], when it is in the power of your hand [yad] to do [asah] it.
27.notes: the chapter turns to the neighbor: the Hebrew reads literally 'from its owners' (baal, H1167) — the good you can do belongs by right to the one who needs it, when you have the means. mana (H4513) is to hold back what should be given. Love that has the power to help and delays is a kind of theft (cf. Jas 4:17). Also tagged: tov (H2896), yad (H3027), asah (H6213).

28.text: When the means are already in your hand, never tell your neighbor, 'Be on your way and return later — I will give it to you tomorrow.'
28.amp: Do not say [amar] to your neighbor [rea — friend, fellow], 'Go, and come again [shub — return, come back], and tomorrow [machar] I will give [natan],' when you have it [yesh — it is present, on hand] with you.
28.notes: rea (H7453) is the neighbor or fellow; the sin is needless delay — 'come back tomorrow' when the help is already in hand (yesh, H3426) today. Generosity deferred for no reason is generosity refused; the wise act while the power and the need overlap (cf. v.27). Also tagged: amar (H559), shub (H7725), machar (H4279), natan (H5414).

29.text: Do not plot harm against your neighbor, who lives beside you trusting in your goodwill.
29.amp: Do not devise [charash — plow, fashion, secretly contrive] evil [ra] against your neighbor [rea], since he dwells [yashab — sits, lives, settles] securely [betach — in trust, without suspicion] beside you.
29.notes: charash (H2790) means to plow or engrave — here to quietly fashion a scheme in the mind. The aggravation is the neighbor's trust: he lives betach (H983), in unguarded confidence, beside you. To plot against the one who trusts you is to betray a peace he never doubted (cf. Ps 41:9). Also tagged: ra (H7451), rea (H7453), yashab (H3427).

30.text: Do not pick a fight with anyone for no reason, when he has done you no harm.
30.amp: Do not strive [rib — contend, quarrel, bring a legal dispute] with a man [adam] without cause [chinnam — for nothing, gratuitously], if he has done [gamal — dealt, brought about] you no harm [ra].
30.notes: rib (H7378) is to contend, even to drag into a lawsuit; chinnam (H2600) means without cause, the same word for the harmless victim in 1:11. The wise man does not manufacture conflict where none is owed — needless quarreling is itself a kind of violence against peace. Also tagged: gamal (H1580), adam (H120), ra (H7451).

31.text: Do not envy the violent man, and choose none of his ways,
31.amp: Do not envy [qana — burn with jealousy, covet] the man [ish] of violence [chamas — cruelty, wrong, lawless force], and choose [bachar — select, prefer] none of his ways [derek];
31.notes: chamas (H2555) is brutal, lawless violence — the sin that filled the earth before the flood (Gen 6:11). qana (H7065) is the burning envy that wishes for what another has; the temptation is to covet the violent man's apparent success. Wisdom forbids both the envy and the imitation: not one of his roads (bachar, H977) is to be chosen. Also tagged: ish (H376), derek (H1870).

32.text: for the LORD detests the crooked man, but the upright are taken into His confidence.
32.amp: for the perverse [luz — the one turned aside, twisted off the true line] is an abomination [toevah — a detestable thing, loathed] to the LORD [YHWH]; but His secret counsel [sod — intimate friendship, the confidence shared among friends] is with the upright [yashar].
32.notes: toevah (H8441) is the strongest word for what God loathes; sod (H5475) is the intimate circle of trusted friends, the secret shared only with the close. The contrast is breathtaking: the LORD recoils from the crooked, yet draws the yashar (H3477) into His own confidence (cf. Ps 25:14; John 15:15). Also tagged: luz (H3868), YHWH (H3068).

33.text: The LORD's curse rests on the house of the wicked, but He blesses the home of the righteous.
33.amp: The curse [meerah — the binding curse, the opposite of blessing] of the LORD [YHWH] is in the house [bayith] of the wicked [rasha]; but He blesses [barak] the dwelling [naveh — pasture, homestead, settled abode] of the just [tsaddiq — the righteous].
33.notes: meerah (H3994) is the active curse, barak (H1288) its mirror-opposite. The two-sided verdict reaches into the home: not only the man but his bayith (H1004) and his naveh (H5116), his whole settled life, falls under blessing or curse. Where the man stands with God, his household stands too (cf. v.32). Also tagged: YHWH (H3068), rasha (H7563), tsaddiq (H6662).

34.text: Toward the mockers He is mocking, but to the humble He gives grace.
34.amp: Surely He scorns [luts — mocks, derides] the scorners [luts — the mockers themselves]; but He gives grace [chen — favor] to the lowly [anav — the humble, the bowed-down and afflicted].
34.notes: the wordplay is exact: God mocks the mockers (luts, H3887) — their scorn returns on their own heads — yet pours chen (H2580) on the anav (H6035), the humble. Quoted twice in the New Testament (Jas 4:6; 1 Pet 5:5) as the law of the kingdom: God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.

35.text: The wise will inherit honor, but fools only lift high their shame.
35.amp: The wise [khakham] will inherit [nachal — take as a lasting possession] glory [kavod — honor, weight, esteem]; but shame [qalon — disgrace, dishonor] is what fools [kesil — the dull, stubborn fool] hold high [rum — lift up, exalt].
35.notes: nachal (H5157) is to inherit as a permanent portion — the wise come into kavod (H3519) as an estate that lasts. The closing line turns bitterly ironic: the kesil (H3684) does rise and is exalted (rum, H7311), but what he lifts up before all is his own qalon (H7036), his shame. The two destinies of the whole chapter — honor and disgrace — close the case. Also tagged: khakham (H2450).
